source.authors: Krupp A, Bertsch B, Spring O
source.title: Costunolide Influences Germ Tube Orientation in Sunflower Broomrape – A First Step Toward Understanding Chemotropism

value: 76 ± 17% of germ tubes within 2 mm of the source grew toward costunolide (10−4 M on the filter paper) against 48 ± 11% in the outer 2–5 mm zone
method: Petri-dish chemotropism bioassay: conditioned O. cumana seeds on 1% water agar around a filter disc carrying purchased costunolide; germ tube curvature toward (+) or away (–) from the disc scored after 5–7 days
conditions: Percentages are shares of oriented germ tubes only: germ tubes with no clear direction (the 'zero group', 0) are excluded from the positive-versus-negative calculation (Figure 3 legend; Results: 'around 70% of the oriented germ tubes' for exudate and oil extracts). Concentration series (Figure 5), concentrations applied to the disc: at 10−7 and 10−6 M positive and negative curving were 'nearly identical' (55 ± 13% and 56 ± 12%), positive reactions 'became evident' at 10−5 M (68 ± 8%) and 10−4 M (76 ± 17%); the Figure 5 legend says active concentrations at the seed surface are 'lower but undetermined'. In the costunolide tests at 10−6 M and below GR24 (10 µl, 1 ppm in water) replaced ddH2O on the disc because germination was too low, so those arms carry GR24 and the legend marks 10−6 and 10−7 M with an asterisk. The strigolactone GR24 (3.3 × 10−6 M on the disc) gave an equal ratio of germ tubes curving toward and away and no significant difference between the two distances (Figure 4 legend: the distance effect holds for costunolide but not GR24). Figure 4: means ± standard deviation of n = 5–7 replications, Tukey test p < 0.05, ANOVA. Standard bioassay: seeds in a concentric circle 2 mm from the 5-mm filter disc, micropyles alternately left and right; the distance comparison (Figure 4) comes from additional experiments, (a) a second concentric circle 4 mm from the disc edge and (b) seeds evenly spread without distinctly positioned micropyles at 0-2 and 2-5 mm from the substance (Methods), so micropyle direction relative to the source was not controlled in the 0-2 against 2-5 mm comparison; dishes sealed and kept dark at 18 C; 10 µl ddH2O added to start diffusion. Costunolide purchased from Selleck Chemicals, dissolved and diluted in methanol; no methanol-only control is described in the Methods. Seeds: O. cumana pathotype G collected in the Rostov region of Russia in 2012 (a wild seed lot, not a cultivar).
quote: Within a distance of 2 mm, 76 ± 17% of the germ tubes grew toward costunolide (10−4 M applied on the filter paper), while in the outer zone (2–5 mm), only 48 ± 11% showed positive chemotropism (Figure 4).
note: Directed germ tube growth of the living parasite toward a host-derived sesquiterpene lactone (a chemotropic response by an intact seedling). Refile after audit 219, which dropped the earlier line for omitting the Figure 5 null, the oriented-only denominator and the GR24 additions; those are carried here. Whether 48% differs from chance is not stated in the sentence. Authors: Anna Krupp, Barbara Bertsch, Otmar Spring (Crossref, issued 2021-08-13, CC BY 4.0, checked in this unit; the PDF states 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'). Names: POWO powo.science.kew.org/taxon/662284-1 (and urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:662284-1) Orobanche cumana Wallr., 'This species is accepted' (opened in this unit); WFO wfo-0000388508, wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-0000388508-2025-06, June 2025 snapshot, 'this species name was accepted by WFO' (opened). source.authors: Ohishi N, Hoshika N, Takeda M, Shibata K, Yamane H, Yokota T, Asahina M
source.title: Involvement of Auxin Biosynthesis and Transport in the Antheridium and Prothalli Formation in Lygodium japonicum

value: average number of antheridia per individual spore was 0.23 ± 0.31 with ABA added to GA4-Me medium against 2.05 ± 0.49 with GA alone
method: dark-grown protonema on GA4-methyl ester medium with and without ABA; antheridia counted per protonema and averaged (Figure 2B)
conditions: Every Figure 2 arm contained GA4-Me (10 or 100 nM per Methods); there is no GA-free control in this figure, so the comparison is ABA plus GA4-Me against GA4-Me alone. The means fall to about one ninth (0.23 / 2.05 = 0.11, computed here); the Results sentence's 'approximately one fifth' refers to the number of protonema carrying antheridia, not to antheridium means. The legend says 'per individual spore' while the Results text calls the 2.05 ± 0.49 (N = 60) the average on individual protonema. ABA concentration: Results text 10 µM, Methods sentence 100 µM for ABA and IAA (unreconciled in the paper). Steel–Dwass test, different letters p < 0.05; N = 60 GA alone, 76 GA + ABA, 44 GA + IAA. The same sentence gives 0 for GA + IAA, which is not logged here: the paper's own reading is that the abnormal protonema shape is not directly linked to disrupted antheridium formation, and no causal claim about IAA is made in this record. For ABA the authors write that antheridia seen on some protonema whose elongation was restricted 'seems to suggest that antheridia formation is not directly suppressed by ABA', and that ABA 'may be concerned with protonema elongation and antheridia formation'; ABA also drastically altered tissue morphology (protonema length 78.02 ± 10.79 µm, about 50% of GA4-Me alone).
quote: The average number of antheridia per individual spore in GA alone, GA + ABA, and GA + IAA were 2.05 ± 0.49, 0.23 ± 0.31, and 0, respectively.
note: Hormone-response experiment on cultured Lygodium japonicum protonema (ABA and GA4-Me applied in the medium). Refile after audit 220, which dropped the earlier line because its quote was the Results sentence while the value used the Figure 2 legend; the quote here is the whole legend sentence. Authors per Crossref (issued 2021-12-09, CC BY 4.0, checked in this unit); the MDPI page was reported as CC BY. Names: POWO powo.science.kew.org/taxon/17143040-1 Lygodium japonicum (Thunb.) Sw., 'This species is accepted' (opened); WFO wfo-0000748052, wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-0000748052-2025-06, June 2025 snapshot, 'this species name was accepted by WFO' (opened).
